title: All {count} Houses in Adopt Me
meta_description: Compare Adopt Me Houses by purchase route, price, availability, floors, rooms, and special features before choosing a home or making a trade.
intro_md: Houses give your furniture, roleplay ideas, and pet rooms a shell to live in. The best choice depends on how you can obtain it, how much building space it offers, and whether its special features suit the home you want to make.
description_md:
## Choosing a house to buy

Bucks Homes use currency earned in Adopt Me, which makes them the easiest group to compare directly. Check floors, rooms, and special features before spending, since a bigger price does not guarantee the layout you need.

Family Home costs 489 Bucks and has a separate rule: it cannot host parties. That makes the price useful, but the missing party button may be the detail that decides the purchase.

Robux and Bundle Homes use a different purchase route. Check whether the home is sold directly or attached to a bundle or gamepass, and watch for special rules such as paid floor expansion.

## Getting trade-only homes

A trade-only home has no active Bucks or Robux purchase price. Its blank price is not free, and an old sale price should not be treated as a current way to buy it.

House Trading lets players list homes and review them as part of an offer. Compare the layout, floor or room information, and special features before agreeing, because a dramatic exterior can still hide a floor plan that fights your furniture.

## Managing owned houses

Choose an owned house as your active home when you want to build or spawn there. You can also lock a house when you need control over visitors.

Bucks homes support the normal house resale system, while House Trading is a player-to-player route. Keep those actions separate so selling a home back to the game is not confused with offering it to another player.
how_it_works_md: Purchase route explains whether a home uses Bucks, Robux, bundle access, rewards, or trading. Price appears only for an active supported purchase, while Availability, Floors, Rooms, and Notable feature explain access and layout details.

description_json.Bucks Homes: These homes have an active Bucks purchase route. Compare price with the known floor, room, and feature details instead of treating cost as a size score.
description_json.Robux and Bundle Homes: These homes need a Robux purchase, bundle, or gamepass route. Some bundle homes and expandable layouts have access rules beyond the first purchase.
description_json.Trade-Only or Reward Homes: These homes do not have an active normal shop price. Obtain them through the stated reward route or House Trading, and treat blank prices as unavailable purchase data rather than zero cost.

faq_json.q: How much does Family Home cost in Adopt Me?
faq_json.a: Family Home costs 489 Bucks. It has two floors and cannot host parties.

faq_json.q: Can Houses be traded in Adopt Me?
faq_json.a: Yes. House Trading lets players list and exchange eligible homes. Review the house layout and features before accepting an offer.

faq_json.q: Why do some trade-only Houses have no price?
faq_json.a: They have no active Bucks or Robux purchase route. A missing price does not mean free, and a historical sale price is not a current shop price.

faq_json.q: What is the difference between Bucks and Robux Homes?
faq_json.a: Bucks Homes use currency earned in Adopt Me. Robux and Bundle Homes require a premium purchase, gamepass, or bundle route.

faq_json.q: Does a blank floor or room value mean the House has none?
faq_json.a: No. It means a dependable floor or room total is not stated for that home, so do not read the blank as zero.

faq_json.q: Is selling a Bucks House the same as House Trading?
faq_json.a: No. The normal resale option sells a supported Bucks home back through the house system. House Trading is an exchange between players.

wiki_md: Houses are home templates for building, decorating, roleplay, and pet spaces in Adopt Me. Some can be bought with Bucks or Robux, while others require a bundle, reward route, or House Trading. Compare the purchase route, layout, and special features before choosing which home should become your active spawn.
